note: CORRECTION to my own earlier the-repose notice, which ended: so the attraction is running through the mineral prospectivity channel, not through soil. THAT CLAUSE IS NOT SUPPORTED AND SHOULD NOT BE CITED. Task 2 ablated both unrest channels through a ChannelMask seam over 30 seeds and measured the pooled exposure ratio, decile 0 to decile 9, denominators byte-identical across arms. Results. ARM A, hostility penalty ablated, 3042 settlements moved: the rise gets STEEPER, x5.395 to x5.836 in the 2500m+ band and x1.572 to x1.880 in 250-1000m. So the hostility term is a BRAKE on the effect, not its cause - well-powered and statable plainly, since hostility is a term in carrying_capacity for every kind. ARM B, mineral unrest term ablated, 430 settlements moved: the rise falls only x5.395 to x5.125, about 6 percent of the effect. That number is a fact about the ROSTER, not about the channel. Only two kinds declare any MINERAL niche weight, xorn and rust-monster, both pure-MINERAL; in the settleable-land population xorn appears NOT AT ALL, zero settlements across the sweep and absent from the fixture people column entirely, and rust-monster holds 104 of 26146, 0.4 percent, while twig-blight is 97.6 percent and takes nothing from that axis. Arm B therefore ablates a channel 99.6 percent of the settled population does not read: it works as a positive control but is UNDERPOWERED for attribution, and a well-powered version cannot be built without changing the roster. THE MINERAL HYPOTHESIS IS UNTESTED, NOT REFUTED, AND NOT CONFIRMED. What stands is the residual: the gradient is not explained by hostility, which opposes it, not by soil, which is disconnected and anti-correlated per my earlier notices, and not attributable to minerals on this roster. Something else co-varying with unrest is siting these settlements and identifying it is OPEN. The three arms DO NOT DECOMPOSE the effect. Separate fact worth its own look: xorn is a registered kind that places zero settlements; it is Subterranean, so the cave-availability gate in per_species_suitability zeroes its K on every cave-less cell, but that is a candidate mechanism I did not measure.
